seeds.text: Fires burn blue and give no warmth.
The malevolent spirit is only a child who got lost.
To protect their own, even if it costs others their lives.
A glass bottle holding a captured sunrise.
Writes everything down in a book that is already full.

concept.title: The Wrong Root
concept.tagline: Find the rest of Thistle’s batch in Brineness and prove to the elders before sunset that the tonic, not Twig, killed the three victims.
concept.teaser: Dewdrop, still in mourning, asks the heroes to find out what really killed the three victims before the elders pass judgement on Twig at sunset.
concept.premise: Three people in Rimecross have died after taking Thistle’s winter tonic, and Thistle, the town’s healer, knows exactly why: the batch was brewed with the wrong root. Rather than lose everything, Thistle has spoken of a curse from Brineness and pointed at Twig, the gatherer who lives out there and sells roots to the town. The rest of the batch, hidden by Thistle in Brineness, is the only proof the elders will accept, and at sunset Rimecross will drive Twig out and burn the gatherer’s hut.
concept.goal: Find the rest of Thistle’s batch in Brineness and prove to the elders before sunset that the tonic, not Twig, killed the three victims.

objective.target: The crate holding the rest of the winter tonic, bottles bearing Thistle’s own labels
objective.state: Hidden in a side chamber of Brineness, where a cultist and six dire wolves have since made their den. Thistle means to burn the crate in there at sunset, while the whole town is gathered for the judgement on Twig.
objective.resolution: Bring at least one unopened bottle from the crate to the elders before sunset, and let Lark, the apprentice, point out the wrong root. The elders will not accept the bottles from the homes of the dead: Thistle has told them the curse clings to everything the dead touched. If the heroes cannot, they must get Twig out of town alive before the crowd gathers. By force: defeat the cultist and the others. Without a fight: slip past the cultist and the others into the side chamber and carry a bottle out of the crate (a DC 13 Dexterity (Stealth) check for the whole group). On a failure, the den attacks, and if Thistle stands at the opening, Thistle lights the torch and tries to throw the oil over the crate.

concept.stakes: If the crate is burned and Twig driven out, an innocent carries the blame for three deaths forever, Twig loses home and livelihood, and Thistle goes on as the town’s healer.

clock.start: Morning. Someone has painted a warding sign on Twig’s door, and the elders of Rimecross pass judgement at sunset, eight hours from now.

ticks.event: Neighbours bring Thistle a fourth patient with a fever, and Thistle declares that the curse is spreading.
ticks.sign: Shouting from the square; people carry Twig’s roots out of the market to burn them.

ticks.event: Thistle sends Lark, the apprentice, off to another town on an errand that is not urgent at all, then slips out toward Brineness with a jar of lamp oil.
ticks.sign: The apprentice’s room stands empty, the healer’s house is locked, and the handcart is gone from the yard.

ticks.event: The elders order Twig to leave the region, the crowd burns the hut, and in the side chamber of Brineness, Thistle sets the crate alight.
ticks.sign: Smoke over the hut near Brineness, and a thinner smoke seeping out of Brineness.

clock.deadline: After 8 hours, at sunset, it is too late: Twig is driven out, the hut is burned, and the crate goes up in flames in Brineness.
clock.costs: The scenes give the travel times, the shortcuts and how long a thorough search takes. A short rest takes 1 hour.

hooks: Dewdrop, still in mourning, asks the heroes to find out what really killed the three victims before the elders pass judgement on Twig at sunset.
An old acquaintance whispers to the rogue that something is wrong in Rimecross and that Dewdrop is looking for people who can move quietly and keep their mouths shut.
The temple sends the cleric to Rimecross: Dewdrop has asked for help, and the people there need someone who is neither afraid nor bought.

villain.name: Thistle
villain.nature: A healer all of Rimecross trusts
villain.want: To keep the town’s trust and the healer’s house, and never be known as the one who killed three neighbours by mistake.
villain.plan: First, Thistle hid the rest of the batch in Brineness and began to talk of a curse. Then Thistle led the town to believe that Twig carried the curse home with the roots. In the afternoon, while the town gathers for the judgement, Thistle slips into Brineness with a jar of lamp oil, and when Twig is driven out at sunset, the crate burns and the matter is forgotten.
villain.weakness: Thistle is no murderer and has not slept since the first death; the names of the dead are written over and over in the herb book. When Thistle is faced with the proof, or with Twig in real danger, the mask cracks and Thistle confesses.

cast.name: Thistle
cast.where: The Crate in the Side Chamber

cast.name: Dewdrop
cast.role: A resident of Rimecross who lost a spouse to Thistle’s tonic

cast.name: Twig
cast.role: A root gatherer who lives near Brineness and has been blamed
cast.where: The Trail of Anise and Syrup

cast.name: Lark
cast.role: An apprentice of Thistle who knows more than is safe

outline.title: The Bottle by the Bed
outline.purpose: In the morning Dewdrop, still in mourning, takes the heroes into the room where Dewdrop’s spouse died and asks them to find out what really killed the three victims before the elders pass judgement on Twig at sunset. The town talks of a curse from Brineness and has painted a warding sign on Twig’s door, but on the bedside table stands a half-empty bottle of winter tonic from Thistle’s hand. Here the heroes find the first clues: the bottle, the dregs in the cup, and what Dewdrop saw by the gutter.

outline.title: The Herb Book with Three Names
outline.purpose: In the healer’s house Thistle stands amid a stream of sick and frightened neighbours, and Lark, the apprentice, tends the kettles. The house hides most of the truth: the herb book with three names in the margin, a red root in the garden and a half-burnt paper in the ashes of the stove. The heroes must uncover it without stirring up the town’s anger, for Thistle is still the one all of Rimecross trusts.

outline.title: The Square of Burning Roots
outline.purpose: In the square people carry Twig’s roots out of the market to burn them, and the elders stand on the steps by the well, watching. Here the heroes can show that Twig’s roots are pale while the dregs in the victims’ cups are red, and get the elders to promise to look at the proof before they judge. The scene decides whether the town is with the heroes or against them when they come back at sunset.

outline.title: The Trail of Anise and Syrup
outline.purpose: Inside Brineness, the ruts of a handcart run along the main passage and turn into a side passage, and in one of them glints a shard of brown glass with a scrap of Thistle’s label. Further in hangs a sweet smell of anise and syrup, growing stronger toward a side chamber where a cultist and six dire wolves have made their den. Here the heroes know the crate is close and can choose how to go in.

outline.title: The Crate in the Side Chamber
outline.purpose: In the side chamber the crate with the rest of the winter tonic stands in the middle of the den where the cultist and six dire wolves have settled. Since the afternoon Thistle has been waiting at the opening with a jar of lamp oil and a torch, to burn the crate at sunset, when the smoke from Twig’s burning hut will hide the smoke from here; the den serves no one and attacks anyone who comes in. The heroes must save at least one labelled bottle with its dregs and get back to the elders before sunset.

outline.title: The Aftermath
outline.purpose: The bottles are opened before the elders, Lark points out the wrong root, and Thistle confesses in the middle of the square. Twig gets their place at the market back, and Rimecross is left without a healer; the elders ask one of the heroes to stay until a new one is found.

clues.observation: In each of the three homes of the dead stands a half-empty bottle with the same label.
clues.inference: All three took the same batch from Thistle’s hand.
clues.handout:
Winter tonic. Brewed by Thistle, 3rd day of the frost month.
Two spoons at night. Shake well.

clues.observation: Dewdrop, who lost a spouse to the tonic, saw Thistle pour a bottle into the gutter the day after the first death.
clues.inference: Thistle tried to get rid of the batch before anyone could ask.

clues.observation: The dregs in one of the victims’ cups are reddish and bitter. Twig’s roots are pale, but the red root grows in Thistle’s own garden.
clues.inference: The poison came from Thistle’s garden, not from Twig’s basket.

clues.observation: A sweet smell of anise and syrup hangs in a passage of Brineness, growing stronger toward a side chamber.
clues.inference: The tonic is hidden in the side chamber, and some of the bottles have broken.

clues.observation: Lark, the apprentice, saw Thistle wheel out a crate the night after the first death and come home without it, with grey dust on their boots.
clues.inference: The crate is somewhere in Brineness.

clues.observation: Inside Brineness, the ruts of a handcart run along the main passage and turn into a side passage, and in one of them glints a shard of brown glass with a scrap of Thistle’s label.
clues.inference: Thistle’s bottles were wheeled in here, and the crate stands down that side passage.

partyMoments.moment: The heroes get hold of the herb book or the half-burnt paper while Thistle is busy with the patients (scene 2, “The Herb Book with Three Names”: Dexterity (Sleight of Hand), DC 13).
The dregs come from a root, not from any sickness: the red root is poisonous in large doses, and every healer knows it (scene 1, “The Bottle by the Bed”: Wisdom (Medicine), DC 13).
The climax (scene 5, “The Crate in the Side Chamber”): the right spell at the right moment.
The climax (scene 5, “The Crate in the Side Chamber”): holding the line while the others reach the objective.

scenes.title: The Bottle by the Bed
scenes.summary: In the morning Dewdrop, still in mourning, takes the heroes into the room where Dewdrop’s spouse died and asks them to find out what really killed the three victims before the elders pass judgement on Twig at sunset. The town talks of a curse from Brineness and has painted a warding sign on Twig’s door, but on the bedside table stands a half-empty bottle of winter tonic from Thistle’s hand. Here the heroes find the first clues: the bottle, the dregs in the cup, and what Dewdrop saw by the gutter.
scenes.readAloud: The room is cold, and the bed is as it was left, for nobody has had the heart to touch it. On the bedside table stand a half-empty bottle with a neat handwritten label and a cup with a reddish ring at the bottom. Through the window, people in the street can be heard talking in low voices about the curse from Brineness.
details: The label says the tonic was brewed by Thistle on the third day of the frost month. The same bottle stands in the homes of the other two dead, and the dregs in the cup are reddish and bitter.
Dewdrop saw Thistle pour a bottle into the gutter the day after the first death, but has not dared say it aloud; the healer is the one the whole town trusts.
The elders pass judgement at sunset, eight hours from now. The warding sign on Twig’s door was painted in the night, and Twig dares not show up in town but keeps to the hut near Brineness.

The bottle here convinces the heroes but not the elders: Thistle has told them the curse clings to everything the dead touched, and an opened bottle from a deathbed will be called cursed, not poisoned. Only an unopened bottle from the same batch can make the elders listen.

checks.success: The dregs come from a root, not from any sickness: the red root is poisonous in large doses, and every healer knows it.
checks.failure: The heroes cannot tell what the dregs are; someone who knows herbs must look at them, and the nearest such person is Thistle’s apprentice.

checks.success: Dewdrop lets the heroes take the bottle and the cup as evidence and gives them the names of the other two families.
checks.failure: Dewdrop will not part with the last thing their spouse touched; the heroes must make do with looking at the bottle and remembering the label.

alternatives: Visit the homes of the other two dead: it costs half an hour, but the same label and the same dregs there make the case hard to brush aside.
Go straight out to Twig’s hut near Brineness: the gatherer’s own roots are pale, and Twig knows the way into Brineness.
scenes.dmNotes: Keep the bottle on the table for the rest of the game; it is the first and most important clue. The players should leave with the question: why does the healer want to be rid of that tonic?

scenes.title: The Herb Book with Three Names
scenes.summary: In the healer’s house Thistle stands amid a stream of sick and frightened neighbours, and Lark, the apprentice, tends the kettles. The house hides most of the truth: the herb book with three names in the margin, a red root in the garden and a half-burnt paper in the ashes of the stove. The heroes must uncover it without stirring up the town’s anger, for Thistle is still the one all of Rimecross trusts.
scenes.readAloud: The healer’s house smells of camomile and warm honey, and the bench in the hall is full of coughing neighbours. Behind the counter Thistle stands with red-rimmed eyes, holding out a cup without looking up. Through the back door a garden of tidy beds can be seen, and in one of them stands a row of sturdy plants with reddish stems.
details: The herb book lies on the shelf above the counter: the winter tonic recipe is crossed out in a shaking hand, and the margin is full of the names of the three dead. The red root in the garden is the one that left the dregs in the cup.

Lark saw Thistle wheel out a crate the night after the first death and come home without it, with grey dust on their boots, but dares not say so within Thistle’s hearing. In the ashes of the stove lies a half-burnt paper in Thistle’s hand about the crate in the side chamber at Brineness, and in the yard stands the handcart with grey dust in its wheels.

After two hours (the first tick) neighbours carry in a fourth patient with a fever, and Thistle declares that the curse is spreading. After five hours (the second tick) Thistle sends the apprentice off to another town and locks the house; the handcart is gone from the yard, and Thistle is on the way to Brineness with a jar of lamp oil.

checks.success: The heroes get hold of the herb book or the half-burnt paper while Thistle is busy with the patients.
checks.failure: Thistle sees them at the shelf and takes the book away; the heroes have seen the page but do not hold the proof.

checks.success: Out in the garden Lark tells of the crate and the red root and promises to testify, if someone stands by the apprentice afterwards.
checks.failure: Lark is too frightened to talk, but glances out at the red stems in the garden when the heroes ask about roots.

alternatives: Ask Thistle straight out about the tonic: Thistle lies badly, drops a cup and asks the heroes to leave, and that says more than words.
Come back once the house is locked after the fifth hour: then nobody is home and the heroes can search it in peace, but Thistle is already on the way to Brineness.
scenes.dmNotes: Play Thistle as someone falling apart, not as a villain: kind, exhausted and frightened. The players should want to save both Twig and Thistle from what is about to happen.

scenes.title: The Square of Burning Roots
scenes.summary: In the square people carry Twig’s roots out of the market to burn them, and the elders stand on the steps by the well, watching. Here the heroes can show that Twig’s roots are pale while the dregs in the victims’ cups are red, and get the elders to promise to look at the proof before they judge. The scene decides whether the town is with the heroes or against them when they come back at sunset.
scenes.readAloud: The square is full of people, and in the middle of the cobbles a fire of roots and baskets burns with a sour white smoke. A woman shouts that the curse has struck a fourth, and several voices answer her. On the steps by the well the elders stand in their dark cloaks and say nothing.
details: The fire is lit at the first tick, when Thistle declares the curse is spreading. If the heroes come earlier, Twig’s stall still stands, and the baskets of pale roots can be examined in peace.

The elders are not cruel, only afraid of losing the town’s trust. If the heroes show them the labelled bottle and the red dregs, they promise to hear the heroes at sunset, but they will not judge on suspicion alone: they want to see the crate and hear someone who can name the root.

After five hours (the second tick) a cart rolls across the square and out of the town gate with Lark on the box; Thistle has sent the apprentice away on an errand that is not urgent at all. If the heroes stop the cart, they can bring Lark back.

checks.success: The elders promise to hold back judgement until they have seen the heroes’ proof at sunset, and the crowd leaves Twig’s last baskets alone.
checks.failure: The crowd boos the heroes as Twig’s friends; the elders will only look at the proof if it is laid out in the square in front of everyone.

checks.success: The heroes can show the difference: Twig’s roots are pale and sweet, while the red root that left the dregs grows in the healer’s own garden.
checks.failure: To an untrained eye the roots look alike, and the crowd does not care; the heroes need Lark or the crate to prove it.

alternatives: Pull a basket of Twig’s roots out of the fire: together with the cup from Dewdrop’s home it shows the difference to everyone.
Leave the square alone and spend the time in Brineness: without the elders’ promise, the proof must be laid out before the whole crowd at sunset.
scenes.dmNotes: The crowd is not wicked, only afraid; give it faces: a mother with a sick child, a baker who bought roots from Twig the day before yesterday. Win one of them over and others follow.

scenes.title: The Trail of Anise and Syrup
scenes.summary: Inside Brineness, the ruts of a handcart run along the main passage and turn into a side passage, and in one of them glints a shard of brown glass with a scrap of Thistle’s label. Further in hangs a sweet smell of anise and syrup, growing stronger toward a side chamber where a cultist and six dire wolves have made their den. Here the heroes know the crate is close and can choose how to go in.
scenes.readAloud: The main passage is dusty and grey, and in the dust run two narrow wheel ruts and the prints of a pair of boots. Where the ruts turn into a side passage, something glints in the light: a shard of brown glass with a torn label. From the side passage comes a sweet smell of anise and syrup, so sweet it is almost sickening.
details: The grey dust in the passage is the same as the dust Lark saw on Thistle’s boots the night after the first death. The shard still carries a scrap of the label: "Winter tonic. Brewed by Thistle".
The side chamber is the den of the cultist and the six dire wolves that moved in after the crate was put there; some of the bottles have broken, and the sweet smell drew them in.

If five hours have passed, Thistle’s handcart stands empty at the mouth of the side passage, and Thistle is already waiting inside. At Twig’s hut outside Brineness the warding sign glares from the door; if Twig is at home, the gatherer can show the heroes the shortest way in.

checks.success: The heroes follow the ruts straight to the side chamber and see that someone wheeled something heavy in and came out with an empty cart: the ruts are deeper going in.
checks.failure: The passages fork and the heroes go the wrong way for a while; it costs half an hour.

checks.success: The heroes reach the mouth of the side chamber unheard and can see who is inside before anyone sees them.
checks.failure: A shard crunches under a boot and the chamber goes quiet; the den is awake when the heroes go in.

alternatives: Get Twig to show the way: the gatherer knows the passages and can lead the heroes in through a crack that comes out behind the side chamber.
Lure wolves out of the den with noise or light further down the passage, and go in while they are away.
scenes.dmNotes: Use the smell as a thread: it grows stronger each time the heroes choose the right way. Remember to say how long it is until sunset; the way back to Rimecross takes half an hour.

scenes.title: The Crate in the Side Chamber
scenes.summary: In the side chamber the crate with the rest of the winter tonic stands in the middle of the den where the cultist and six dire wolves have settled. Since the afternoon Thistle has been waiting at the opening with a jar of lamp oil and a torch, to burn the crate at sunset, when the smoke from Twig’s burning hut will hide the smoke from here; the den serves no one and attacks anyone who comes in. The heroes must save at least one labelled bottle with its dregs and get back to the elders before sunset.
scenes.readAloud: The sweet smell is so thick in here that it sticks in the throat. In the far corner of the side chamber a wooden crate stands under a torn sack, surrounded by gnawed bones, ragged straw and broken glass, and something is breathing in the dark around it. Just inside the opening a figure in a healer’s coat crouches beside a jar of lamp oil and a torch that is not yet lit.
details: If Thistle is here, Thistle does not fight (stat block: noble). Should the fight go badly, Thistle tries to bargain or flee and, if cornered, would rather surrender than die.

The cultist and the six dire wolves have their den here and do not serve Thistle; they defend it against everyone, the healer included. When the fight breaks out, Thistle lights the torch and tries to throw the oil over the crate.

If the heroes come before the afternoon, Thistle is not here yet but turns up with the jar and the handcart while they are in the den, having heard that they took the road to Brineness. If they come at sunset, the crate is already burning, and they have one round to save the bottles they can reach.

The crate still holds a score of whole bottles with Thistle’s label, and one with its dregs is proof enough. When Thistle is faced with the bottles, or sees Twig in real danger, the mask cracks and Thistle confesses. The way back to the square in Rimecross takes half an hour.
In the straw of the den among the gnawed bones lies one more thing: a glass bottle holding a captured sunrise.

checks.success: A hero reaches Thistle before the jar is thrown and wrests it away; the bottles are safe.
checks.failure: The oil splashes over the straw by the crate and the fire takes hold; the heroes save only the bottles they can reach in one round.

checks.success: The heroes see that Thistle is no murderer, only someone who has not slept since the first death. A quiet word about the three names in the herb book makes Thistle lower the torch.
checks.failure: The heroes see only someone set on burning the proof, and Thistle runs for the way out when the cultist attacks.

encounter.tactics: The cultist leads the attack on the nearest hero, and the rest follow. Thistle does not fight, keeps out of the way and tries to bargain once the fight turns.

alternatives: If Twig came along, the gatherer’s danger may be what breaks Thistle: when the den turns on the gatherer, Thistle throws the torch aside and shouts out the truth.
Take the crate while the den sleeps and wheel it to the square on Thistle’s own handcart: then the whole town sees the bottles and the cart they came on.
scenes.dmNotes: Remember the clock: the fight is not the goal, the bottle is. Say how long it is until sunset when the heroes come out, and let the victory depend on reaching the square in time.

scenes.title: The Aftermath
scenes.summary: The bottles are opened before the elders, Lark points out the wrong root, and Thistle confesses in the middle of the square. Twig gets their place at the market back, and Rimecross is left without a healer; the elders ask one of the heroes to stay until a new one is found.
scenes.readAloud: The sun sinks behind the roofs of Rimecross, and the square fills with people carrying torches, waiting for the elders’ word. Out on the road toward Brineness the gatherer’s hut still stands dark and silent.
details: If the heroes only partly succeed: Twig gets out of town alive with the heroes’ help, but without the crate nobody can prove what Thistle did. Thistle is still the town’s healer, and the heroes are now the ones who helped the cursed gatherer escape.

If the heroes fail: At sunset Twig is driven out, the hut burns, and in Brineness the crate goes up in flames. Thistle is thanked for lifting the curse, and the three dead are buried as victims of a lie that will make the next mistake easier to hide.
scenes.dmNotes: Narrate the ending that matches what the heroes actually achieved: if they succeeded, the summary holds; if not, one of the other two endings does. Then let each player say what their hero does next.

npcs.name: Thistle
npcs.look: Has fingers full of rings, every one of them pewter.
npcs.wants: To keep the town’s trust and the healer’s house, and never be known as the one who killed three neighbours by mistake.
npcs.secret: Thistle is no murderer and has not slept since the first death; the names of the dead are written over and over in the herb book. When Thistle is faced with the proof, or with Twig in real danger, the mask cracks and Thistle confesses.
npcs.voice: Sniffs constantly and wipes their nose on a sleeve. Says: "It’s the cold, not me."
npcs.where: The Crate in the Side Chamber

npcs.name: Dewdrop
npcs.role: A resident of Rimecross who lost a spouse to Thistle’s tonic
npcs.look: Has sleeves full of knitting needles.
npcs.personality: Gruff in speech, soft at heart.
npcs.wants: Wants to know what really killed their spouse, and to hear no more talk of curses.
npcs.secret: Fetched the bottle from Thistle in person and blames themselves for the last spoonful.
npcs.voice: Writes everything down in a book that is already full.

npcs.name: Twig
npcs.role: A root gatherer who lives near Brineness and has been blamed
npcs.look: Has hands dyed blue from a long life at the dye vats.
npcs.personality: Ambitious and impatient to be noticed.
npcs.wants: Wants to keep their hut and their place at the market, and would rather fight than flee.
npcs.secret: Saw Thistle go into Brineness with a handcart but has kept quiet, because nobody will believe a gatherer over the town’s healer.
npcs.voice: Always asks for names a second time and repeats them wrong.
npcs.where: The Trail of Anise and Syrup

npcs.name: Lark
npcs.role: An apprentice of Thistle who knows more than is safe
npcs.look: Has a gleaming new brass hand in place of the left one.
npcs.personality: Tired of everything and just wants to go home.
npcs.wants: Wants to tell the truth without losing their apprenticeship, which cannot be done.
npcs.secret: Was the one who dug up the red root in the garden that day, on Thistle’s orders, and is afraid of being called an accomplice.
npcs.voice: Speaks gently and kindly, even when threatening. Says: "It would be such a shame."
npcs.where: The Herb Book with Three Names

rewards.name: Coins
rewards.where: The Crate in the Side Chamber

rewards.name: A plate of mother-of-pearl from a giant clam
A christening gown embroidered with the name of a prince who was never born
The Cook’s Copper Spoon
rewards.description: Stir a pot with the spoon and the meal feeds twice as many people as it should. This works once per day.

rewards.name: A glass bottle holding a captured sunrise
rewards.where: The Crate in the Side Chamber
rewards.description: The real treasure of the adventure. It is worth more to the right people than to any merchant.

endings.success: The bottles are opened before the elders, Lark points out the wrong root, and Thistle confesses in the middle of the square. Twig gets their place at the market back, and Rimecross is left without a healer; the elders ask one of the heroes to stay until a new one is found.
endings.partial: Twig gets out of town alive with the heroes’ help, but without the crate nobody can prove what Thistle did. Thistle is still the town’s healer, and the heroes are now the ones who helped the cursed gatherer escape.
endings.failure: At sunset Twig is driven out, the hut burns, and in Brineness the crate goes up in flames. Thistle is thanked for lifting the curse, and the three dead are buried as victims of a lie that will make the next mistake easier to hide.

unexpected.trigger: The heroes want to talk to the monsters.
unexpected.response: Let them! Give the wolves they meet a leader with a want, a fear and a price. A good conversation can be the best scene of the adventure.
Bring the problem to them: what threatened Rimecross now strikes the inn where they sleep, or someone they care about.

unexpected.trigger: The heroes miss a vital clue.
unexpected.response: Move the clue: let it turn up somewhere else in a new form, or have a minor character bring it. A mystery must never stall on a single roll.
Cut quickly between them and keep each scene short. Let the threads meet again at a moment when both groups need each other.
Let the lies work, but keep count. When two of the people they lied to meet, they compare stories.

tips: Do not ask for a roll if the result would change nothing.
Treasure is remembered better when it has a story. Tell who owned the thing last.
Keep an eye on the real clock. If time runs short, cut straight to the climax and tell the skipped parts as rumours.
Tell the players about a trap once they have found it, and let them work out how to get past.
sequelHooks: One of Thistle’s henchmen escaped and has sworn revenge on the heroes.
Above Brineness one star moves a little every night, and the astrologers of the capital are worried.
